correctness.rationale: For every odd prime, Lucas factorization is derived termwise from the binomial sum; D_0=D_(p-1)=1 and the Legendre recurrence exclude adjacent zero digits. The carry digit rule is an iff, yielding the exact geometric count at every p^L. The degree-m hypergeometric differential equation modulo p is invariant under X->1-X; coefficient uniqueness and H_m(1)=(-1)^m imply H_m(1-X)=(-1)^m H_m(X). For p=3 mod 4, odd m implies H_m(-1)=0, so D_m=H_m(2)=0 modulo p. Arbitrary-cutoff monotonicity gives error O(N^alpha) with alpha<1, and infinitely many such primes give gcd growth in density. The packaged standard-library checker returned VERIFY_OK for 24 primes and 70 complete digit blocks; finite checks supplement rather than replace the proof. No unsolved infinite premise or external computational certificate is used.

originality.rationale: The final claim is the exact all-prime adjacent-Delannoy gcd digit-count formula plus its density-one divergence corollary. Sun (2010) proves reciprocal weighted sums and basic Delannoy congruences; Sun (2016) proves polynomial identities and supercongruences; Lengyel (2021) treats special prime-power-indexed values and differences; Rowland-Yassawi (2013) supplies general automatic/Lucas-congruence methods. OEIS A001850 records sequence data, not the neighboring gcd invariant. Actual exact-claim and alias searches in research records and open literature returned no matching result. Established ingredients are not misrepresented as new. A stronger theorem or unindexed equivalent remains a residual risk, not a proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed paper or equivalent corollary of a more general Lucas/Deuring theorem may already state the final gcd-density result.

value.rationale: The arithmetic invariant gcd of consecutive central Delannoy numbers is naturally motivated by an integer lattice-path counting sequence. Exact exceptional counts at all prime-power digit lengths and explicit power-saving exponents establish fine correlation information. More importantly, common divisors exceed every fixed bound with density one, in sharp qualitative contrast to classical second-order divisibility sequences with coprime neighbors. No artificially chosen cutoff or tiny computational improvement is used.
